Mathematician Richard Schwartz has proven that a doughnut-shaped surface, or torus, can be formed from a flat sheet of paper through a complex folding technique involving triangles. His research indicates that a torus can be created with eight vertices but not with seven, and he utilized both computer simulations and artificial intelligence to assist in his analysis. This work builds on decades of origami mathematics and establishes new parameters for possible origami constructions.
